**ORBIT ZERO: MISSION EARTH** is an educational space exploration game designed to make learning about Earth and space science more interactive, engaging, and accessible. Players take on the role of astronauts completing four main missions based on real-world space exploration challenges, followed by five more difficult Special Quests. Throughout the game, players explore space, overcome obstacles, complete scientific tasks, and collect Jade to upgrade their own Main Ship.

Project Details – ORBIT ZERO: MISSION EARTH

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

ORBIT ZERO: MISSION EARTH is an educational space exploration game that turns space science into an interactive experience. Players take the role of astronauts and explore a futuristic Space Hub, where they can access missions and manage their Main Ship.

The game includes four Main Missions that introduce the core gameplay, followed by five more challenging Special Quests. Players complete objectives, explore environments, overcome obstacles, and earn an in-game currency called Jade. After completing each Main Mission, they receive a new ship part that can be used to upgrade their Main Ship.

2. What are its benefits?

The project makes learning about space more engaging and accessible. Instead of only reading scientific information, players can interact with the game environment and learn through missions. It also encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, curiosity, and decision-making.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to encourage students, especially young learners, to become more interested in Earth and space science. We want to show that scientific learning does not have to be limited to textbooks. It can also be interactive, enjoyable, and inspiring.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

The project is designed as a web-based game. Our planned development tools and technologies include:

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript/TypeScript: For the website structure, interface, and game logic.
  • Three.js: For creating 3D environments, space objects, and interactive visual elements.
  • React and Vite: For building and managing the web application.
  • Visual Studio Code: As the main development environment.
  • NASA.gov: As a reference for scientific information and real-world space exploration concepts.

5. How is the project creative?

ORBIT ZERO combines space exploration, educational missions, and spaceship customization into one connected experience. Its futuristic 3D Space Hub gives players a place to explore between missions, while the Main Ship progression system makes their achievements feel meaningful.

The combination of four main missions, five advanced Special Quests, and a Jade-based upgrade system creates a sense of progression beyond a traditional educational quiz or presentation.

6. What factors did the team consider?

During the design process, we considered:

  • Educational value: Scientific information should be meaningful and understandable.
  • NASA relevance: Mission concepts should connect with real space science and reliable NASA information.
  • Accessibility: Gameplay should be understandable for students without advanced scientific knowledge.
  • Difficulty balance: Challenges should be engaging without becoming too difficult.
  • Creativity and engagement: Visual design, exploration, and progression should motivate players.
  • Technical feasibility: The game should be realistic to develop using accessible web technologies.

Ultimately, ORBIT ZERO aims to connect education and entertainment, helping students discover the excitement of space science through interactive exploration.
